publication.title: Long COVID as a Chronic Multisystem Disorder: Pathogenesis, Persistence, and Therapeutic Perspectives
publication.abstract: In October 2021, the WHO defined Long COVID, or post‐acute sequelae of SARS‐CoV‐2 infection (PASC), as a condition characterized by symptoms that persist for at least two months, typically beginning three months after the acute infection and not attributable to alternative diagnoses. Long COVID is now recognized as a chronic, multisystem disorder encompassing more than 200 reported symptoms across respiratory, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, neurological, and systemic domains. Increasing evidence indicates that persistent SARS‐CoV‐2 activity within sanctuary tissues—including lymphoid organs, the gastrointestinal tract, and the olfactory neuroepithelium—may sustain chronic inflammation and immune dysregulation long after viral clearance from the upper airways. Persistent viral proteins can disrupt cellular homeostasis, impair organelle function, and trigger apoptosis, while endothelial dysfunction has emerged as a central driver of systemic manifestations. Detection of sub genomic viral RNA, residual viral proteins, and sustained antigenemia supports the hypothesis of ongoing low‐level replication or delayed clearance in a subset of patients. Such persistence may also facilitate reactivation of latent herpesviruses, particularly Epstein–Barr virus (EBV), which establishes lifelong latency in B lymphocytes. EBV reactivation has been increasingly documented during acute COVID‐19 and may contribute both to severe disease endotypes and to post‐acute symptoms such as fatigue, cognitive impairment, and neuropsychiatric disturbances. This review synthesizes current evidence linking viral persistence, immune dysregulation, endothelial injury, mitochondrial dysfunction, and herpesvirus reactivation as interconnected mechanisms driving Long COVID pathogenesis, highlighting the need for targeted diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

The Relationship Between Physician Assistant Self-Efficacy and Leadership Style
publication.abstract: Abstract The current study explored the relationship between physician assistants’ self-efficacy and leadership style. Participants included a total of 163 physician assistants in the United States. Self-efficacy was reported using the General Self-Efficacy Questionnaire (GSE) by Schwarzer and Jerusalem and leadership style was evaluated using the Multifactor Leadership Questionnaire (MLQ-5X) by Bass and Avolio. Autonomy was measured using the Independent Practice and Support Subscale of the Nurse Practitioner Primary Care Organizational Climate Questionnaire (NP-PCOCQ) by Poghosyan et al. A demographic survey included items relating to gender, age, ethnicity, and years of experience. After controlling for the demographic variables, multiple regression results indicated that self-efficacy significantly predicted leadership behaviors in physician assistants. Positive relationships were found between leader self-efficacy and self-reported transformational leadership (explained 21.2% of the variance) and transactional leadership (explained 12.2% of the variance). The results suggest that physician assistants with the self-regulation of thought processes, motivation, and self-confidence may engage in increased transformational and transactional leadership behaviors. These findings may inform leadership development among physician assistants by focusing on building self-efficacy in physician assistant students and practitioners.

SARS-CoV-2: Potential feco-oral transmission and implications on the spread and severity of COVID-19 in Venezuela. Mini-review
publication.abstract: The recognized human-to-human transmission of SARS-CoV-2 is through respiratory droplets and contact with contaminated surfaces. However, the high transmissibility of the virus and the pattern of symptoms of COVID-19 suggest the likelihood of other forms of spread. Increasing evidence suggests that SARS‐CoV‐2 could be transmitted by the feco‐oral route. SARS-CoV-2 is known to infect gastrointestinal epithelial cells and a significant number of infected people have gastrointestinal symptoms. Viable viruses, viral RNA, and prolonged shedding of viral RNA have been detected in the feces of COVID-19 patients. The virus has been found in sewage and surface waters of several countries. The possible feco-oral transmission of SARS-CoV-2 could be significant in low-income countries. High poverty levels and the collapse of health and other public services might increase the risk of Venezuelans to suffer a more devastating impact from COVID-19 than other populations. In conclusion, the feco-oral transmission of SARS-CoV-2 has not been demonstrated. However, it is conceivable and the impact of COVID-19 could be high in low-income countries, especially in Venezuela due to its humanitarian crisis. The lack of information on the viability and infectivity of the virus in wastewaters and surface waters and the risk of transmission of the infection are important gaps in knowledge that deserve further investigation.

publication.publisher: HSOA Journal of Physical Medicine, Rehabilitation, and Disabilities
publication.abstract: The purpose of this study was to examine attitudes toward the voluntary practice of eugenics among people with high-risk inheritable diseases and genetic disorders. Participants consisted of 426 students attending two large public universities in the south and southwestern regions of the United States. The study used the modified scale of attitudes toward mental retardation and eugenics, the risk-taking questionnaire, and the dimensions of religious ideology importance scale. A general linear model was tested to answer the research question. The results showed that the model was significant (p < 0.001; adjusted r2 of 0.078). Significant main effects were found in race [F (4,378) = 2.538, p = 0.04, η2 = 0.026], risk avoidance [F (1,378) = 12.536, p < 0.001, η2 = 0.032] and importance of religion [F (1,378) = 5.530, p = 0.019, η2 = 0.014]. Cultural, ethnic, and religious variables influenced people’s views toward disability. One’s perception of both disability and its impact on quality of life will influence his or her feelings about eugenics and babies with congenital conditions.

Due to a chronic shortage of mental health providers, much of the burden of mental health care in rural areas have shifted to the primary health care sector. UTRGV proposes to enhance mental health education and training to 100 first year PA students, 80 second year PA students and another 80 capstone PA students. The UTRGV Department of Physician Assistant is proposing to address and offer solutions to these concerns with this grant proposal. Specific objectives: Objective I. Since the opening of our PA program, our graduates have transformed healthcare delivery in our region by practicing in the medically underserve communities where they have been trained. grant.abstract: UnlockED: An Escape Room Learning Toolkit for Higher Education Angelica Urbina, Christina Gonzles and Nathalie Chacon Gamified learning strategies are increasingly used in higher education to promote student engagement and application of knowledge. This proposal seeks to develop UnlockED, an openly licensed Escape Room Learning Toolkit designed as a PDF reference manual with visuals and step-by-step instructions to guide faculty and educators in creating and implementing effective educational escape rooms as an active-learning strategy. The project builds on the authors' extensive experience designing and implementing both classroom-based and digital escape rooms across multiple courses to support collaboration, problem-solving, and application-based learning. Currently, these escape room activities exist as instructor-specific implementations; this project addresses the need for a structured, step-by-step Open Educational Resource (OER) that guides others through the design, facilitation, and curricular integration of escape rooms. The proposed toolkit aligns with the UT System's Curricular Innovation through OER Grant Program by advancing open pedagogy, reducing barriers to adoption of active-learning practices, and supporting scalable curricular innovation. The applicant team brings demonstrated expertise in curriculum design, gamified instruction, and digital resource development, positioning them with the capacity to successfully develop, implement, and disseminate a sustainable toolkit.

presentation.title: Back to the Pitt
presentation.abstract: An unforgettable, high-impact educational adventure where emergency medicine meets immersive learning. “Back to the Pitt” is a dynamic, hands-on workshop designed specifically for PA students and early career PAs. Based on the fictional medical drama The Pitt, participants are thrown into a fast-paced ED shift with cases that test their clinical reasoning, teamwork, and time management under pressure. Created by experienced ED PAs, this workshop weaves real-life emergency cases into collaborative puzzles and clues. Students must work as a team to analyze vitals, interpret diagnostic data, and solve both medical and logic-based challenges to escape before time runs out. This workshop promotes critical thinking, active learning, and camaraderie—mirroring the high-stakes world of emergency medicine while keeping it engaging and memorable. A short debriefing at the end of the presentation, helps tie up any lose ends and helps solidify the knowledge gained. Learning Objectives: 1. Identify key clinical findings and red flags in common emergency medicine presentations. 2. Interpret essential diagnostic data such as EKGs, imaging reports, and lab values under time-sensitive conditions. 3. presentation.abstract: Evidence suggests a potential EBV-associated severity endotype in COVID‐19, with PCR-defined EBV reactivation commonly reported in severe/ICU populations, but with substantial heterogeneity across studies and specimen types. Across included reviews/meta-analyses, there was no pooled OR/RR/HR specifically linking PCR EBV DNAemia to subsequent development of PASC/Long COVID, indicating an important evidence gap at the umbrella-review level [bmj, 2017], [Su Y, 2022], [Talukder, 2024]. [Su Y, 2022], [bmj.com, 2017], [Su Y, 2022]. presentation.title: Decoding Long COVID: Risk Factors, Proteomics, and Treatment
presentation.abstract: Abstract: Long COVID or Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC), is a chronic disorder characterized by persistent symptoms and health issues following SARS-CoV2 infection. This conference aims to provide a comprehensive overview and new theories of Long COVID, focusing on its definition, diagnosis criteria, symptoms, risk factors, and pathophysiology. We consider that Long COVID is a systemic disorder that includes the endothelial tissue as its modulator of the disease expression, viral persistence in patients with prior conditions, autoimmunity, and coagulopathies are part of the underlying pathology. We will explore the natural history of the disease, proteomic insights, and both conventional and non-conventional treatment approaches. Long COVID requires a full study to understand the best treatment option based on the infection timeline, which risk factor defines progression to Long COVID and prognosis biomarkers. Finally, we will discuss future steps in research and clinical practice to manage better and understand this condition. Purpose of Presentation This interdisciplinary presentation aimed to advance understanding of Long COVID by integrating virology, immunology, proteomics, and clinical treatment strategies. It emphasized the importance of early diagnosis, biomarker identification, and personalized care approaches. Key Scientific Contributions Pathogenesis & Immunopathophysiology: Long COVID is characterized by persistent viral presence, immune dysregulation, oxidative stress, endothelial damage, and mitochondrial dysfunction. The disease affects multiple organ systems and is driven by cycles of inflammation, thrombosis, and autoimmunity. Risk Factors Identified: Female sex, middle age Severe acute infection Low vitamin D levels EBV reactivation Comorbidities Protective Factors: Vaccination Early antiviral therapy Physical activity Vitamin D sufficiency Proteomics & Biomarker Discovery Proteomic analysis revealed host-virus protein interactions and novel therapeutic targets. Key biomarkers include IL-6, TNF-α, CRP, HMGB1, low taurine, and mitochondrial damage indicators. The interactome of SARS-CoV-2 proteins with host pathways (e.g., ACE2, TMPRSS2, NRP1) was mapped to guide future drug development. This presentation is part of a broader research initiative and will contribute to the future peer-reviewed publications.

presentation.abstract: Traditional healthcare has been characterized as a field where professionals work independently, creating an environment with multiple providers in multiple locations duplicating services, adding to the ineffectiveness and waste of resources. The fragmentation of healthcare provision promotes isolation, competition, and attempts to preserve power among professions. Accordingly, patient care is less than optimum. To begin to ameliorate this situation Interprofessional Education has been developed. However, a significant part of this education is effective interprofessional collaboration (IPC) which creates higher patient satisfaction, better coordination of patient care, efficient use of healthcare services, and higher professional job satisfaction. Furthermore, the World Health Organization has made collaboration a priority based on Health Ethics. The purpose of this research is to determine the differences in healthcare professionals’ perceptions of IPC, demographic factors related to IPC, and what dimensions and aspects of IPC healthcare rate the highest. The significance of this survey research is the provision of information and a starting point for the groundwork for the interprofessional education of pre-health care professionals. The participant sample consists of physician assistants, nursing, occupational therapists, communication sciences and disorders, health, and biomedical sciences, health, and human performance, social work, cooperative pharmacy, and rehabilitation counseling. The Perception of Interprofessional Collaboration Model-Questionnaire (PINCOM- Q) is the survey instrument used in this study. Keywords: Interprofessional collaboration, interprofessional education, global, healthcare, fragmentation, healthcare ethics

presentation.title: The Relationship Between Physician Assistant Self-Efficacy and Leadership Style
presentation.abstract: By considering physician assistants’ self-efficacy and leadership style, this study examines whether self-confidence plays a role in physician assistants’ performance of tasks and responsibilities or whether Self-efficacy determines Leadership behaviors (Transformational, Transactional, and Passive Avoidant Leadership). In addition, age, gender, ethnicity, years of practice experience, and autonomy will determine any impact on leadership behavior. For this study, a convenience sample of 2,608 practicing physician assistants from the Texas Academy of Physician Assistants, Rio Grande Valley PA Society, Bexar County PA Society and the Texas Pediatric Physician Assistant Society were asked to complete a 4-item demographic survey, the 36-item Multifactor Leadership Questionnaire, the 9-item General Self-Efficacy Scale, and a 10-item Autonomy scale. Participants included a total of 163 practicing PAs in the United States.The research design included a non-experimental design in this study in order to collect and analyze data determining the relationship between Self-Efficacy and Leadership style. The relationship was measured by a demographic survey and three survey instruments. The demographic survey included items relating to gender, age, ethnicity, and years of experience. The Multifactor Leadership Questionnaire (MLQ) evaluated the self-reported leadership behaviors of physician assistants, the General Self-Efficacy Scale (GSE) evaluated the self-rated self-efficacy of physician assistants, and the Independent Practice and Support Subscale was used to evaluate physician assistants’ self-reported autonomy. In this non-experimental research study, descriptive statistics were used for Self-Efficacy, the dimensions of Transformational, Transactional, and Passive Avoidant Leadership, including their respective facets, and control variables encompassing gender, age, ethnicity, years of experience, and autonomy. All continuous variables were analyzed with Pearson r correlations and the statistical analysis of this study included multiple regression. Confidence levels were established at 95% (p < .05).

presentation.abstract: The Rio Grande Valley has a very rich Hispanic culture. In an effort to help the PA students transition into medical Spanish, I took the beloved game of Lotería (Mexican bingo) and reimagined it into a fun and interactive way to begin learning some medical Spanish. Using a game to teach anatomy in Spanish became a "win-win" for me and my students as it took the pressure off of spending hours of vocabulary memorization and created a fun way to expose the students to both Spanish medical terminology and Hispanic culture. After piloting this project with two consecutive PA classes in their orientation week, the feedback from the students was overwhelmingly positive. In conclusion, this game could potentially be modified to suit any subject matter for the health professions student and beyond.

presentation.title: Effect of Study Methodology and Self-Efficacy on PACKRAT Scores
presentation.abstract: Purpose: Effective study methods may vary but are required for college success specifically in intense programs like the physician assistant program. Individual versus group study methods have been under debate with some results more in favor of group study. This difference was not evaluated within physician assistant programs particularly after the application of team based learning method (TBL). The aim of this study is to evaluate study habits of PA students, their perceived benefits for each study method, their perceived self-efficacy for self-regulated learning and the association with their PACKRAT score. Methods: An online survey was developed and sent to PA students assessing their study methods, personality type, and their perceived self-efficacy for self-regulated learning using Banadura’s self-efficacy scale. Descriptive and regression analyses were conducted using STATA 14. Results: Respondents (N=54) were mainly females (74%), with a mean age of 30 (±6) years old and 35.8% reported being visual learners. Half of the respondents preferred to study individually while 3.7% preferred group study and 46.3% reported both individual and group study. 80% reported studying individually is effective when compared to only 50% reporting group study is effective. Respondents were 75% -85% confident regarding their self-regulated learning methods used and 43.4% used repetition as their method of memorization technique. Mean Packrat score was 146.8 (±18.4, range 102- 195). Mean Packrat score was not significantly different by study methodology. Additionally there was no significant correlation between Packrat scores and any of the self-efficacy measures. Simple and adjusted linear regression did not reveal any significant relationship between study methodology and Packrat score. Discussion: Though the study did not reveal any significant relationship between study methodology, perceived self-efficacy for self-regulated learning and the PACKRAT score yet this can be attributed to the small sample size. A similar study is needed across various PA programs in order to increase the study sample size.
